text: Hi everyone, nice to see you again.Welcome to today's English class.Please get your student's book and the worksheet ready.In the last three lessons, we read three different poems.Today, I have a new poem for you, but most of the time you need to learn through listening.First, let's warm up with a chant.What is a chant?A chant is something like a song.A rhyming poem with quite a lot of repetition in it.That means when you read or sing the chant, you repeat some words or lines a lot.So you can feel the rhyme and rhythm when you read it aloud.The first task for you today is to listen, write down the words you hear to complete the chant on your worksheet.It's task one.Get your pens ready.Focus.Three, two, one, go.The racing chant.Look at those kids.Look at them run.This is exciting.This is fun.Look at that skier.Look at her go.She's not slow.I'm excited.Got all the words down?Let's check the answers.Since it's chant, it has rhyming words.And the rhyming words are these.Do you get the same words?Besides, what words or lines are repeated in this chant?Take a look.They are, look at, like, look at those kids and look at the skier.This is, this is exciting and this is fun are repeated several times.Also the line, I'm excited and she's.Thus, repetition is created.Let's talk about the subject.Which pictures match the subject of the racing chant?There are picture A and B.The running kids and the woman skier.They are all racing with others.Got warmed up?Good.Today, we'll listen to a new poem.Can you guess the subject or the topic of it?Perhaps a typhoon.Have you experienced a typhoon?Or have you seen any movies or video clips about a typhoon?When a typhoon comes, what may happen?There will be damage, right?But where?What places?Let's brainstorm.Write down as many keywords as possible.You can do it on your worksheet.Task 2.Time's up.How many have you come up with?Let me remind you that actually we learn about typhoon in book 6B.Do you remember the picture?We can see in the streets.Trees are blown down.Rubbish is everywhere.The trees are all over the place.Plastic bags, paper flying in the air.Tough work for the street cleaners.And windows are broken maybe by the falling or flying objects out of nowhere.Think about being outside during a typhoon.Broken glass of windows will be a great danger.Your umbrella can be blown away.You will feel it hard to walk in the street.And you yourself are almost blown away too.Isn't it dangerous to stay outside on typhoon days?Shops and stores are closed.See the sign in the picture?It is almost blown off.Have you ever heard of the blown off advertisement boards which hurt passersby?What terrible news!How about the ships and boats sailing at sea?Big waves may sink ships and boats.Damage or even disasters like shipwrecks may happen.And of course, to our flats.Heavy objects may be blown off and may fall on cars or even hurt people.So we better not put things like flower pots outside on the balcony.Perhaps you have more ideas when talking about typhoon.And if it is a poem writing about a typhoon, what will be described?This is Benny's poem.However, there are some mistakes in it.What we have to do today is to listen to the poem, spot the mistakes and correct them.But no hurry.Let's look into the text to get familiar with it.Open your textbook.Turn to page 118.First, read and tell.How many verses are there in the poem?There are six.Is it a rhyming poem?In fact, the question is a little tricky because there are some mistakes in the poem.Is it possible to find out the answer?See verse one.July is an incorrect word.It should be May.May and way.They rhyme.And see the repetitive use of the word away.May, way and away.So probably it is a rhyming poem.And it can be a clue for us to find the mistakes.Read through the poem.Use a pencil.Underline the possible mistakes.You can do it in your textbook.What words have you marked?My student Claire would like to share her ideas with you guys.I take much notice of the rhyme in this poem.If it is a rhyming one, then round in verse two is probably not correct becauseIt doesn't rhyme with may, way and away.It should be a rhyming word.Well, I guess it should be a color with the sound a.That's the same with home and table and sandwiches.Perhaps they're round two.Besides, the week in the last verse, it is also a mistake.Thanks to Claire, we can find out the answer.Yes, I noticed something else.The line, there are planes in the harbor.How can there be planes in the harbor?So probably there's something wrong with plane or harbor.And the word houses in verse five is odd.The word there in the next line must refer to houses.Eating the houses' sandwiches.How can a house eat anything?Hmm, neat ideas.Thank you, Sam.What about you, boys and girls?Have you found anything else?It's time for you to listen and write.Listen to the recording of the poem.Cross out the mistake and write the correct word next to it.We'll listen twice.Take your time.The signal is up.Although it's just May.A typhoon is coming.It's coming this way.There are ships in the harbor.Some blue and some gray.But a typhoon is coming to blow them away.There were people at work and people at play.Now the typhoon is here.They've all gone away.A waiter was holding ten plates on a tray.But the typhoon came quickly and blew them away.There were horses in Lantin just eating their hayWhen the typhoon came in and blew it away.Now the typhoon has gone.Thank goodness, we say.And we won't have another for many a day.How is it going?I have the answers for you.Let's check.First, planes in the harbor should be ships in the harbor.Brown should be gray.Clear guessed right.It is a color with the sound A.At home should be at play.What does at play mean?Play is a noun here.And people at play means people who are playing outside.At home and at play are something like a parallel here.平行结构It helps create rhythm.Table in line 14 is a mistake.It should be tray.But what is a tray?The waiter in the picture is holding a tray.托盘Usually, a tray is used by waiters to hold plates, bows and other stuff.Can you imagine a waiter holding ten plates on the tray at a time?A tall pile of plates, right?He must be a skillful waiter.Any other mistakes in this verse?Yes, came slowly should be came quickly.Not a slow or long process of coming.We talked earlier about the word houses.Yes, it is incorrect and should be horses.Sam is careful enough to notice the possible mistake here.Good job.Actually, house and horse are similar in pronunciation and spelling.It can be a common error.By the way, Lenten is the name of a place where there are many horses being raised.Sandwiches, as we predicted, is wrong and should be hay.The horse in the picture is eating his hay.The last one is week.It should be day with a rhyming sound.You may wonder what many a day means.It means many days.That's the same with many a week, which means many weeks.Since days don't rhyme with say, the writer uses many a day instead.Do you get all the correct words down?Did you guess right?Here we have the right version of Benny's poem, a typhoon.Now let's read it aloud after the recording.Ready?Although it's just May, a typhoon is coming.There are ships in the harbor, some blue and some gray.Now let's read closely to find out more about this poem.What is each verse mainly about?The main element in the last verse is we.What about the other five?Think about it.Got the answers?Verse 1 is about the signal.But what might be the signal?I think it might be the signal of the typhoon like big wind, maybe heavy rain, to warn people about the coming typhoon.Verse 2 is about ships at the harbour.Verse 3 is about people.Verse 4, a waiter who was holding a pile of love plates.Verse 5, horses whose hay was blown away, right?And the last one focuses on we.The poem describes how different people in different places were like in the typhoon.Can you divide the whole poem into three sections?A hint for you.Think about the time frame, the progress of the typhoon.Boys and girls, have you got the answer in mind?Actually, the first two verses go in the first section, before the typhoon.Notice the tense here.Is coming is the present continuous tense, but is used to talk about the future.It means will come.Together with to blow, it indicates the typhoon is something in the future, which is not yet to come, but will come.Then, what about the second section?Verses 3 to 5 should go into the middle part.See the verbs here?Typhoon is here.So, what about the people when typhoon has come?Are there people at work or at play?Take a look at the tense.See the tense here?That means there are now no people going to work or hanging outside.Remember what we talked about earlier?It can be very dangerous staying outside.And in the waiter and the horse verses, past tense is used.Everything such as the plates and the hay was blown away into the past.So this section, verses 3 to 5 show what the speaker sees during the typhoon.Obviously, the last verse is the last section of the poem after the typhoon.The present perfect tense has gone means the typhoon is not here any longer.We won't have another one.The future tense here indicates that people are looking into the future to talk about the next typhoon about to come.Now we've seen that the whole poem shows the whole process of the typhoons coming and leaving.So, what feeling or experience is the speaker sharing?Different sections may show different feelings or experience.Read and think about it in mind.These answers are for your reference.The first section shares a feeling of anxiety.The speaker makes a prediction of what will happen.The middle section, it seems the speaker shows us the vivid pictures of the disastrous, the powerful typhoon.It's like we are also experiencing a typhoon.It creates an immersive experience for the readers.What about the last section?What feeling does the speaker share?See the line, thank goodness, we say in the poem.How would you be feeling when you say thank goodness?It's a feeling of relief.So far, we've known the subject of the poem, which is a typhoon, a natural disaster.We've also looked into the feeling or experience the poem shares.Now I would like you to go back to the rhyme.It is a rhyming poem, isn't it?In the previous lessons, we talked about the rhyme.In the previous lessons, we talked about how a rhyming poem makes you feel.Kind of energetic, active, excited, right?But what is the effect of the rhyme and rhythm here?Does it have anything to do with the subject or the feeling and experience?We can feel that rhyme and rhythm push the poem along.They add fun and a sense of playfulness to the poem.But what about the content?The subject is a natural disaster, something dangerous and not so much fun.And there's the feeling of anxiety and the experience of seeing such a great mess.So we say the form of the poem contrasts with the content of the poem.That's something interesting I find in Benny's poem.It could be that the speaker is saying,Yes, a typhoon is terrible.It affects our lives in an awful way.But it's a part of life and life just goes on.We can live it through and even find fun in it.Lastly, let's go back to the raising chen we listened to at the very beginning.Actually, a chen is very useful in poem reading.It uses rhythm and rhyme in an enjoyable way.It provides patterns that can make learning easier.It offers opportunities for repeated readings which can help to build the fluency.And it offers you the chance to write new verses.So why not try rewriting the poem to make it a chen?You can use something in the poem we learned today.What language can you learn from the poem?Make it repetitive in your chen.This is for your reference.And don't forget about the rhyme.Time is up, everyone.My student Michael would like to share his work with us.Thanks to Michael.Very good job.It's
